name: CYPRUS

flag.title: Flag of Cyprus
flag.note: White field, copper island, olive branches

lead: Cyprus is a sun-drenched island in the eastern Mediterranean where Aphrodite, goddess of love, was said to rise from the sea. It gave the world the word for copper — mined here for thousands of years. Today it is a small, friendly republic of beaches, mountains, and the world's oldest named wine, where cats outnumber people.

facts.label: Capital
facts.sub: Only divided capital in the world

geo: Cyprus sits at the crossroads of Europe, Asia, and Africa in the warm eastern Mediterranean. The Troodos Mountains rise through the centre, topped by Mount Olympus at 1,952 m — high enough to have a ski resort.
A flat, sun-baked plain called the Mesaoria stretches between the mountains and the northern Kyrenia hills. Cyprus enjoys over 300 sunny days a year — one of the sunniest places in all of Europe.
animals: The Cyprus mouflon is a stocky wild sheep with great curling horns, found only in the Paphos forest on the Troodos slopes. Once nearly extinct, its numbers have recovered to about 3,000 — it is the national animal.

The cat snake hunts at night and has eerie vertical pupils, just like a cat's. Cyprus is also famous for its huge street-cat population — around 1 million cats live on the island, comfortably outnumbering its people.
culture: Halloumi is Cyprus's squeaky, salty cheese that can be grilled without melting. Made in village kitchens for centuries, it is now EU-protected as uniquely Cypriot and exported worldwide.

Every spring, the Kataklysmos festival turns coastal towns into water-fight arenas, blending ancient sea-god traditions with Christian celebration. Boat races, music, and grilled halloumi fill the harbours.
history: Copper was mined in Cyprus as early as 2500 BC — the island was the ancient world's biggest supplier. The Latin word for copper, cuprum, comes directly from the island's own name, Kypros.
Aphrodite's legendary birthplace at Petra tou Romiou drew pilgrims for centuries. Romans, Byzantines, Crusaders, and Ottomans all ruled here before Cyprus became an independent republic in 1960.
wows: Cyprus is one of only two countries whose flag shows a map of itself — the other is Kosovo.
Commandaria is the world's oldest named wine — made in the Troodos hills since at least 800 BC.
The world's oldest known pet burial was found here: a cat interred beside its owner 9,500 years ago.
Dwarf elephants and pygmy hippos once lived on Cyprus — their fossils have been found across the island.
Up to 20,000 flamingos winter at Larnaca Salt Lake, turning its shores bright pink from November to March.
The world's oldest perfumes — 4,000 years old, scented with lavender and rosemary — were dug up in Cyprus.
Nicosia is the last divided capital on Earth, split by a UN buffer zone through its walled centre.

myths.myth: Cyprus is too hot to visit in summer
myths.fact: The coast is very hot (38°C+), but the Troodos Mountains stay cool, and sea breezes make evenings perfect for outdoor dining and fresh fish.
Halloumi is firm, layered, and made to be grilled — unlike feta it has a high melting point, turning golden outside and chewy inside.
